text:
sam: Quick microbench dump — noticed a consistent tail bump when the host parser and grpc frame coalescer both run.

taylor: Can you paste the perf output?

sam: Pasted below. baseline vs with-parser-opt. small synthetic requests (p50/p95 in ms):
```
baseline: 1.8 / 6.2
parser-opt: 2.3 / 8.0  (+28% p50, +29% p95)
gx: grpc-write overhead ~0.9ms per small frame (observed)
KV: kvcache hot-shard hit-rate drops from 92% -> 71% during the run
```

anya: Oof, that hit-rate drop stands out. Did the test include kernel-selection churn?

sam: Yes — runtime was switching kernels for short sequences due to seq_len heuristics. Every kernel swap triggers small JIT path and extra memcpy. I think that behavior is creating microbursts that evict cache entries.

mike: Do we have a flame graph? Could be PTI + memcopy hot path.

sam: Uploading a trimmed flame snippet:
```
ingress_parser::parse_frame  40%
grpc_writev  12%
memcpy  9%
kvcache::lookup  8%
other  31%
```

zach: That memcpy % is suspicious for small writes. Are we doing per-token copies in host preproc?

sam: We are. There's a small-copy on frame assemble in parse_layer when we normalize chunk boundaries. For large requests it's amortized; for many tiny chat tokens it's not.

anya: Also note the kernel-selection: when seq_len toggles 32->64 we choose a different kernel that uses a different scratch layout, forcing reinit of kv-facing structs. That likely increases churn and coldness in kvcache hash lanes.

perf-bot: New commit 3a9f2b pushed to eng-runtime: reduce-kernel-churn heuristic (PR #4123). Benchmark queue scheduled.

mike: Nice. Did the benchmark run against dedicated capacity or local sim?

perf-bot: Benchmark ran on dedicated-staging (c5-gpu-small). Workload: 10k tiny requests/sec, 75% short seq (<=32), 25% 64 tokens.

sam: Preliminary numbers: after disabling kernel auto-swap for short sequences (+pin small kernel to seq<=48): p50 1.9ms, p95 6.5ms, kvcache hit 89%. Improvement but not full fix. grpc-write still adds 0.6-0.8ms per frame.

taylor: Could we aggregate small frames into a single writev before submission to gRPC? That would reduce syscall overhead (and smallwrite penalty) but might add a little serialization cost.

sam: Tried writev with a 256B coalesce window. Results: p50 1.7ms, p95 5.9ms, but tail variance increases when coalesce delay > 0.8ms. Tradeoff looks promising with adaptive coalesce.

anya: Another angle: change parsing to avoid extra memcpy by using zero-copy slice references during proto decode. That should drop memcpy from 9% to ~2%.

zach: That plus kernel pinning + adaptive writev might push kvcache hit back to >90% and reduce p95 under 6ms. Could be a release candidate.

mike: Any regressions on throughput? Coalescing could harm high-concurrency customers. Need a per-tenant adaptive policy.

sam: Agreed. Proposal: 1) implement zero-copy proto decode (spike) 2) kernel-pin heuristic for sequences <=48 3) adaptive writev with per-route thresholds 4) monitor kvcache eviction rate and roll out as canary to 10% traffic.

taylor: Sounds good. Can you file an RFC and include perf numbers + rollout plan? I'll take kernel-pin patch review.

sam: Filing RFC now: https://redwood.internal/rfcs/eng-runtime/host-chunk-grooming-2026 (draft). Will attach raw benchmarks and flame graphs.

perf-bot: Canary scheduled: eng-runtime/staging -> canary-10pct at 1828243000.

anya: If anyone hits odd regressions, tag me. I'll watch kvcache telemetry and KvEvictAlarm.

sam: Thanks — will follow up with a trimmed checklist. :thumbsup:

zach: Also add a small test harness to simulate tokenized chat workloads (lots of tiny frames) to catch future regressions early.

sam: Added to backlog (ENGRT-711).

mike: Nice work. Short-term wins look feasible.

sam: I'll post a follow-up after the zero-copy spike completes.
